title: Atomic Prompt Transaction (APT) — sketch
content:
Quick scratchpad for an "Atomic Prompt Transaction" concept — rough API + runtime semantics. Goal: let clients submit a multi-step prompt/update sequence that should be applied atomically with respect to local KV cache and model-visible context, and to provide clear failure modes and idempotency so clients can retry without corrupting conversation state.

Motivation / examples:
- multi-turn assistant flow that must update a user profile blob only if the whole generation succeeded (e.g., extract structured data and then persist)
- prompt orchestration pipelines (parse -> enrich -> generate) where intermediate KV writes shouldn't be visible until commit
- client-side optimistic updates + server-side durable commit for private deployments

Primary constraints:
- latency-friendly: common fast-path should be single-request commit+generate (no multi-RPC for happy path)
- consistent with streaming responses: allow streaming tokens while transaction is pending/committed, without exposing uncommitted writes to other concurrent requests
- rollbackable: if commit fails, runtime must be able to revert any cache changes or mark them invisible
- idempotent: retrying a transaction (client crash + retry token) must not double-apply side-effects

High-level model (runtime view):
- APT = {transaction_id, operations[], commit_policy} applied against a session (session_id).
- operations[] are typed: write_kv(key, value, ttl?), delete_kv(key), upsert_blob(id, blob), annotate_prompt(range, label), schedule_fallback(model_variant)
- Each APT has an isolation level: "snapshot" (reads see snapshot at start), "read-committed" (reads see committed writes), "serializable" (strongest, expensive). Default: read-committed.
- Transactions are ephemeral by default: autocommit on success, auto-rollback on explicit failure or timeout. Optional durable commit to customer storage (for Private deployments).

API shape (single-request preferred flow):
POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/transactions
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <key>
  APT-Retry-Token: <opaque-client-token>  // for idempotency
Body (json):
{
  "transaction_id": "client-uuid-1234",
  "isolation": "read-committed",
  "operations": [
    {"op": "write_kv", "key": "last_extract_v1", "value": "{...}", "ttl": 3600},
    {"op": "annotate_prompt", "start": 0, "end": 120, "label": "user-intent"}
  ],
  "generate": {
    "model": "rw-2b-opt",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "stream": true
  },
  "commit_policy": "atomic"  // atomic | best_effort | noop
}

Response (200 on success):
- Begins streaming tokens (if stream=true) as usual
- Final metadata chunk includes {"transaction_commit": "applied" | "rolled_back" | "pending" , "transaction_id": "..."}

Failure modes and semantics: ensure idempotency + observable state
- If network failure after server accepted tx but client didn't receive final metadata: client retries with same APT-Retry-Token. Server must detect previous completion and respond with same outcome (and optionally replay final metadata).
- If server fails during commit: if commit partially applied, runtime must be able to roll back to pre-transaction snapshot or mark txn as failed and hide partial writes. For "best_effort" policy, runtime records applied ops and returns which succeeded.
- For streaming: tokens can be emitted before commit completes; but other concurrent requests must not see uncommitted kv writes. If streaming shows intermediate values that depend on uncommitted state, this is inconsistent — so disallow reads-from-uncommitted within the same session except for the originating request's generator.

KV semantics and cache integration:
- Maintain per-session speculative layer: uncommitted writes stored in a per-transaction overlay. Reads from the same request see overlay; other requests read base+committed only.
- On commit: materialize overlay into base cache atomically (atomic replace of keys or writeset apply). Implementation options: compare-and-swap base version, or use per-key generation numbers.
- Rollback: discard overlay. For durable commit option, append to an ordered commit log (for audit) and then apply.

Concurrency examples (ascii diagrams):
Case A: two parallel generates concurrently
Client A: POST APT(txn=A)  -> runtime creates overlay A -> starts generate (streaming tokens)
Client B: normal generate -> should NOT see overlay A writes until txn A commit
Sequence:
[base kv v1] <- overlay A writes -> (not visible)
If A commits: base kv v2 -> B later sees v2

Sequence diagram:
Client -> Server: POST /transactions (txn=A + generate)
Server -> Model: tokens (stream)
Server (overlay A) [holds writes]
Client -> Server: poll/other req
Server -> Client: returns base-only values (no overlay)
Server -> Server: commit overlay -> atomically swap into base

API for transactional introspection + recovery:
GET /v1/sessions/:session_id/transactions/:transaction_id -> returns status {created_at, status, applied_ops[], outcome}
POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/transactions/:transaction_id/commit -> force commit (idempotent)
POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/transactions/:transaction_id/rollback -> force rollback (idempotent)

Implementation tradeoffs (notes):
- Option 1 (in-memory overlays): low-latency, good for hosted API, but risk losing overlays on node crash unless durable replication. Needs replication across serving nodes for HA.
- Option 2 (WAL + read-through): write transaction ops to WAL immediately, stream tokens while WAL pending fsync, then apply to cache; durable but higher latency.
- Option 3 (async commit + compensating actions): accept transaction, stream tokens, commit asynchronously and notify client via webhook / callback. Simpler but gives eventual consistency and more failure complexity.

Edge cases and unresolved questions (to discuss):
- Size limits: what if operation set is large (e.g., big blobs)? Probably disallow in single APT or require multipart upload to object store + reference write op.
- Compatibility with model rollouts: if model variant fallback occurs mid-stream, should txn commit be canceled? option: keep commit independent — transaction final outcome attached to final generation outcome.
- Multi-session transactions (cross-session): do not support initially. Could be future feature with global locking.

Quick back-of-envelope: performance expectations
- Happy-path single-node hosted: overlay creation + memstore writes ~ sub-ms to low-ms; commit using CAS should be ~1–3ms per small writeset. WAL path adds ~5–20ms depending on fsync and replication.

Open TODOs for next pass:
- Sketch exact wire format for streaming metadata chunk (schema + examples)
- Decide default isolation (I lean read-committed) and document vulnerability windows
- Prototype in serving-runtime with ephemeral overlays (eng spike) and Linear ticket APY-512 for the spike
- UX: SDK helper that auto-manages APT-Retry-Token and exposes high-level commit/rollback helpers

Notes to self:
- See related: session-affinity-and-snapshotting-notes, conversation-checkpoint-format-proposal (need to link when done)
- Quick experiments: spin up a local runtime instance and try overlay apply pattern using per-key version tokens (compare_and_set semantics)

Example minimal client pseudocode (JS):
const txn = await fetchPOST(`/sessions/${sid}/transactions`, {
  transaction_id: txnid,
  operations: [ {op:'write_kv', key:'profile_v1', value: JSON.stringify(extract)} ],
  generate: {model:'rw-2b', stream:true}
}, {headers: {'APT-Retry-Token': token}})
// stream handler sees tokens, waits for final metadata chunk {transaction_commit:'applied'}

Rough risk matrix:
- Incorrect rollback -> data loss (high)
- Double-apply on retry -> duplicate side-effects (medium)
- Increased tail-latency from WAL -> bad for PLG onboarding (medium)

End of scratchpad — target: share with Omar/Maya next week, fast prototype after design alignment.
